title: FieldPoly batch_mul + batch_gcd
description:
Two batch primitives for `FieldPoly<F>` using a balanced product tree and pairwise reduction.

## API

- `pub fn batch_mul(polys: &[Self]) -> Self` via balanced binary product tree (fold-by-pairs).
- `pub fn batch_mul_with_field(sample: &F, polys: &[Self]) -> Self` — same, but caller provides a `&F` so the `polys: []` case can return `FieldPoly::one_like(sample)` without needing any element from the slice.
- `pub fn batch_gcd(polys: &[Self]) -> Self` via pairwise `fold(gcd)`. Explicit in the story spec as "pairwise reduction".

## Success criteria

- Proptest: `batch_mul(polys) == polys.iter().fold(one, |a, b| a*b)`.
- Proptest: `batch_gcd([a*d, b*d, c*d])` divides `d`.
- Unit tests: empty slice, single-element slice for both.
- Bench showing `batch_mul` beats left-fold schoolbook when inputs are balanced.
- `cargo fmt` / `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` / `cargo test --release` clean.
